parabole.definition: Coined by Apollonius in I.11 from Euclidean application of areas (VI.27–29): the square on the ordinate QV equals the rectangle applied exactly along the latus rectum PL with width equal to the abscissa PV (y² = px), neither exceeding nor falling short.

elleipsis.definition: Coined by Apollonius in I.13 from Euclid VI.28: the square on the ordinate QV equals a rectangle applied to the latus rectum p with width PV, falling short (ἐλλεῖπον) by a figure similar and similarly situated to the rectangle contained by the transverse diameter d and parameter p: y² = px − (p/d)x².

hyperbole.definition: Coined by Apollonius in I.12 from Euclid VI.29: the square on the ordinate QV equals a rectangle applied to the latus rectum p with width PV, exceeding (ὑπερβάλλον) by a figure similar and similarly situated to the rectangle contained by the transverse diameter d and parameter p: y² = px + (p/d)x².

orthia.headword: orthia / par' hēn dynantai (ὀρθία / παρ' ἣν δύνανται)
orthia.definition: The 'upright' fixed segment PL erected perpendicular to the diameter at the vertex P against which the rectangle equal to the square of the ordinate is applied; determined by the cone's axial triangle geometry (e.g., p = 2b²/a along the principal axis of a central conic).

plagia.definition: The segment PP' intercepted on the cutting plane's diameter between the two generators of the axial triangle (internal for the ellipse, external across the opposite cone napes for the hyperbola), forming with the orthia p the 'figure' (εἶδος) of the section.

eidos.definition: The rectangle d · p contained by a transverse diameter PP' (= d) and its corresponding parameter PL (= p); for the principal axis AA', one-fourth of the figure equals d·p / 4 = CB² = b², which governs both the asymptote slope and the focal application.

tetagmenos.definition: A straight line QV drawn from a point Q on the conic parallel to the tangent at the vertex P of a chosen diameter (hence bisecting parallel chords), meeting the diameter at V; not restricted to right angles except when the diameter is a principal axis.

diametros.definition: Any straight line bisecting a family of parallel chords of a conic is a diameter; two diameters are conjugate when each bisects all chords parallel to the other (equivalent to mutual polarity with respect to the line at infinity).

hypenantia.definition: In an oblique scalene circular cone, the second family of circular plane sections (I.5 [Heath p. 4]) inclined antiparallel to the circular base across the axial triangle ABC so that ∠AKH = ∠ABC, proving that an oblique circular cone possesses two distinct parallel families of circular sections.

antikeimenai.definition: Apollonius's revolutionary recognition (I.14, I.16) that when a plane cuts both napes of the double cone, the two resulting hyperbolic branches share a single transverse diameter, center, conjugate diameter, and common pair of asymptotes—forming one unified algebraic curve.

symptoma.definition: The invariant planimetric relation linking every point's ordinate QV and abscissa PV on the curve once severed from the 3D generating cone; the direct ancient counterpart of the algebraic equation of an affine curve.

asymptotoi.definition: Constructed in II.1 by setting off PL = PL' on the vertex tangent with PL² = ¼ p·d and joining the center C to L, L': straight lines that never meet the hyperbola at any finite distance yet approach nearer to it than any assigned distance (II.14), satisfying xy = const in asymptotic coordinates (II.12).

semeia-ek-tes-paraboles.headword: ta ek tēs parabolēs ginomena sēmeia (τὰ ἐκ τῆς παραβολῆς γινόμενα σημεῖα)
semeia-ek-tes-paraboles.translation: the points arising out of the application (foci)
semeia-ek-tes-paraboles.greek: τὰ ἐκ τῆς παραβολῆς γινόμενα σημεῖα
semeia-ek-tes-paraboles.definition: Apollonius's technical name in III.45–52 [Props. 69–73] for the two foci S, S' on the major/transverse axis AA' determined by applying a rectangle AS · SA' = ¼ p_a · AA' = b² (falling short by a square for the ellipse, c² = a² − b²; exceeding by a square for the hyperbola, c² = a² + b²). Because a parabola lacks a center C and second vertex A', this 2-vertex application does not apply to it.

topos-pros-treis-kai-tessaras-grammas.headword: topos pros treis kai tessaras grammas (τόπος πρὸς τρεῖς καὶ τέσσαρας γραμμάς)
topos-pros-treis-kai-tessaras-grammas.translation: locus with respect to three and four lines
topos-pros-treis-kai-tessaras-grammas.greek: τόπος πρὸς τρεῖς καὶ τέσσαρας γραμμάς
topos-pros-treis-kai-tessaras-grammas.latin: locus ad tres et quattuor lineas
topos-pros-treis-kai-tessaras-grammas.definition: The celebrated locus of a point P whose oblique distances d₁, d₂, d₃, d₄ to four given lines satisfy d₁·d₃ = λ d₂·d₄ (or d₁·d₃ = λ d₂² when two lines coincide); Apollonius states in Preface I that Book III (Props. 53–56) finally yields its complete synthesis after Euclid achieved only a partial special case.
topos-pros-treis-kai-tessaras-grammas.heath_loci: Preface I, Intro Ch. V, III.53–56 [Props. 74–76], pp. lxx, cxxxviii–cl, 119–125

diorismos.translation: determination of limits of possibility / discriminantal threshold
diorismos.definition: The rigorous determination of the exact parameter bounds separating zero, one (double/tangent), or two real solutions—reaching its supreme ancient expression in Book V Props. 51–52 [Prop. 99] (the evolute discriminant separating 2 vs. 3 vs. 4 normals) and in Book VII's inequality theorems created for Book VIII.
diorismos.heath_loci: Prefaces V & VII, V.51–52 [Prop. 99], pp. lxxv–lxxvi, 168–179

evolute.translation: cuspidal threshold curve separating 4-normal and 2-normal domains
evolute.definition: Although Apollonius has no single noun for the curve as a locus, Book V Props. 51–52 [Prop. 99] construct for every abscissa x the exact critical ordinate y below which 4 normals pass through (x, y), on which 2 normals coalesce, and above which only 2 normals exist—yielding point-for-point the semicubical parabola 27py² = 4(x − p/2)³ and the astroidal Lamé curve (ax)^(2/3) + (by)^(2/3) = (a² − b²)^(2/3).
evolute.heath_loci: Intro pp. lxxv–lxxvi, cxxvii–cxxix; V.51–63 [Props. 99–106], pp. 168–186

epaphai.definition: Apollonius's two-book analytic treatise summarized in Pappus Synagoge VII: given any three elements each being a point (P), straight line (L), or circle (C), construct a circle tangent to all three (10 cases: PPP, PPL, PPC, PLL, PLC, PCC, LLL, LLC, LCC, and the crowning CCC case with up to 8 solutions).
epaphai.heath_loci: Intro Part II Ch. I; Pappus Synagoge VII

neusis.definition: Inserting a straight segment of given length between two given lines or circles so that its prolongation verges through a given pole; Apollonius restricted his two-book treatise On Inclinations strictly to those neuseis constructible by plane means (straightedge and compass).
neusis.heath_loci: Intro pp. cxxv–cxxix; Pappus Synagoge VII
